_what: Published work this project should cite or test itself against, found but NOT YET READ.
_why: Migrated from the chemoqbit register on 15 Nov 2026, when mental illness became its own project. Every entry reached this project through a working synthesis, a search snippet or somebody else's reference list. A citation discovered second-hand is a lead, not a fact.
_how_to_clear_an_entry: Open the publisher PDF, check the claim, set verified_against_publisher_pdf true and record what it actually says in `verified_says`. If the claim does not survive, say so there rather than deleting the entry.
_provenance_warning: These entries came from the USER'S OWN working synthesis, not from a published reference list, and that note says of itself: 'This is a working synthesis; structural data are sparse and the assignments below should be checked against the primary papers.' So they are one step further from verified than the rest of this file, not one step closer.
_why_it_matters: A working synthesis supplied on 14 Nov 2026 proposed DISC1, TRIOBP-1, CRMP1, NPAS3 and dysbindin-1 as a possible next direction. Recorded so it is not lost. NOT QUEUED, and the reason is structural rather than editorial: see _why_the_method_does_not_reach_it.
_why_the_method_does_not_reach_it: Every interface this project computes starts from deposited ATOMIC COORDINATES of a sheet-against-sheet contact. The synthesis states there is no cryo-EM structure of brain-derived DISC1 and no fibril data at all for TRIOBP-1, CRMP1 or NPAS3. The one structural result (Cukkemane 2021) is ssNMR plus EM on a recombinant construct, which gives a core RANGE and not the coordinates of a mating interface. No coordinates, no E_int. The field is roughly where amyloid was before Nelson 2005 (1YJP).
_why_sequence_scoring_is_the_wrong_answe: The synthesis proposes sequence-based aggregation scoring for DISC1 and then refutes it: TRIOBP-1's aggregation-critical 25-residue stretch was called 'unpredicted' by its own authors and was found by testing recombinant fragments. A predictor run here would produce a number with nothing to check it against, in a field that has no structures to check it against. That is the opposite of what this project is for.
_the_one_transferable_asset: Cysteine chemistry. als_approach.py (the Cys6 approach to the Cys57-Cys146 disulfide, with its ~31 kcal/mol disease-timescale bound) and chalcogen_exchange.py (six S/Se thiol-disulfide exchange variants on disk) compute thiol chemistry and need NO fibril structure.
_the_arithmetic_that_blocks_it_first: The DISC1 cysteine motif is C680, C682, C684. The construct reported to form fibrils is 691-836, with the beta-core at 716-761. 680, 682 and 684 are all LESS THAN 691, so the triad sits outside the fibril-forming construct entirely -- not merely outside its core. Before any cysteine machinery is pointed at DISC1, somebody must establish whether those residues are anywhere near the aggregating region. This is arithmetic on the synthesis's own numbers and it is the first thing to check.
_a_correction_recorded_here_so_it_is_not: The synthesis closes by suggesting 'electronic structure of metal sites in SOD1' fits 'your existing SOD1 book and FPGA disease study'. Three separate strands are joined there that are not joined on disk: pd_copper_site_exposure.py computes SOLVENT ACCESSIBILITY (Shrake-Rupley), not electronic structure, under a PARKINSON'S hypothesis (Rowlands, copper-deficient histidine oxidation) rather than ALS aggregation; the FPGA/VQE pipeline is on 5-fluorouracil / thymidylate synthase and formamide, and SOD1 appears nowhere in it; and the 'SOD1 book' is the steric-zipper work on segments 30-35 and 147-153. In a grant or a paper that sentence would be wrong.

entries.citation: Cukkemane A, et al. (2021). Solid-state NMR and EM of a recombinant DISC1 C-region.
entries.claim_as_cited: DISC1 691-836 forms symmetric oligomers and amyloid-like fibrils; beta-core at 716-761; aggregation exergonic with negative enthalpy change; aggregates spread between cultured cells without killing them
entries.action: SUPERSEDED. It yields neither coordinates nor a deposited core range. The whole DISC1 structural corpus is 4 PDB entries, 1 EMDB map and 1 BMRB entry, carrying 75 helix records and ZERO strand records between them; the one multi-chain entry, 9RUX, is a native all-helical coiled-coil tetramer whose model stops at residue 707 and so never reaches the reported beta-core.
entries.CORRECTION_2026_11_15: NOTHING WAS DEPOSITED: no coordinates, no chemical shifts, no EM map, no accession of any kind, and the paper carries no Data availability section. The EM was NEGATIVE-STAIN TEM at 120 kV with no resolution reported, and the 'structure' is a MODELLER protomer docked by CLUSPRO into that envelope. The shift assignments are self-described as 'likely assignments based on proximity to the solution NMR signals'. So the 716-761 beta-core is a DOCKING RESTRAINT, not a measurement, and the paper's own two statements of its boundary disagree (716-761 against 717-761). The 2025 follow-up (J Struct Biol X 11:100128) says verbatim 'No data was used for the research described in the article', has no EM at all, and calculates its 5.73 nm fibril diameter from ssNMR assuming a circular cross-section. Also: that paper cites PDB 5YIH for the murine C-region; 5YIH is a bacterial nucleoside diphosphate kinase. The intended entry is 5YI4.

entries.citation: Trossbach SV, et al. (2016). DISC1 multimerisation and insolubility under elevated cytosolic dopamine, transgenic rat.
entries.claim_as_cited: elevated cytosolic dopamine increases DISC1 multimerisation and insolubility; polymorphisms S704C and L607F increase aggregation in vitro; DISC1 proposed as a sensor of cytosolic oxidative stress
entries.CORRECTION_2026_11_15: L607F IS A TRAP and should not be carried into a structural aggregation analysis. It appears in neither Cukkemane paper. What the 2025 paper discusses is L807-FS, a frameshift downstream of residue 807 -- a different residue and a different lesion. L607F's characterised phenotype is disrupted nuclear targeting and reduced ATF4 interaction (Hum Mol Genet 2012), with no aggregation structure behind it.

entries.citation: Bradshaw NJ, et al. (2017). Aggregation-critical regions of TRIOBP-1.
entries.claim_as_cited: the aggregation-critical region narrows to a 25-residue stretch, described by the authors as 'unpredicted' and found by testing recombinant fragments rather than by prediction
entries.note: This is the entry that argues AGAINST sequence-based scoring, so it is the one to read first if that idea returns.

entries.citation: Samardzija B, et al. Cells 12(14):1848 (2023), PMC10378145. Insoluble CRMP1, DISC1, TRIOBP-1 and NPAS3 in insular cortex.
entries.claim_as_cited: transcribed into this project as 'insoluble proteins in SCHIZOPHRENIA brain tissue' -- which is wrong, see below
entries.note: The brain-tissue half of that claim argues against DISC1 as a seed in patients, which is the opposite of what the cell data suggest. Read both halves before quoting either.
entries.found_in: user working synthesis, 14 Nov 2026; corrected 15 Nov 2026 against the cohort description
entries.CORRECTION_2026_11_15: THE COHORT CONTAINS NO SCHIZOPHRENIA CASES. 33 donors: 15 suicide, 11 control, 4 major depression, 3 Alzheimer. Western blot only, against four pre-chosen proteins; no proteomics, no sarkosyl, no amyloid dye, no seeding assay. No fold changes, no p-values and no FDR are published for the brain data; a donor was called positive at 1.5x the cohort mean. 9/15 suicide (60%) and 5/11 controls (45%) were flagged, which is Fisher exact p = 0.69, odds ratio 1.7 (95% CI 0.4 to 7.8) -- computed here from the reported counts, not published. The authors call it a proof of concept. It does not establish a case-control difference and must not be cited as schizophrenia evidence.

entries.claim_as_cited: a C-terminal cysteine motif (C680, C682, C684) binds arsenous acid with low micromolar affinity and the protein changes function under oxidative stress; a direct link between cysteine chemistry and aggregation is UNTESTED

entries.citation: Garbuzynskiy SO, Lobanov MY, Galzitskaya OV (2010). FoldAmyloid: a method of prediction of amyloidogenic regions from protein sequence. Bioinformatics 26(3):326-332. doi:10.1093/bioinformatics/btp691
entries.claim_as_cited: FoldAmyloid is one of the four legacy predictors that failed on TRIOBP-1 in Bradshaw et al. 2017, and its server is unreachable, so half the legacy baseline cannot be re-run.
entries.action: READ IN FULL 15 Nov 2026, and it splits into two claims that must not be stated as one. (1) THE SERVER IS GONE. The paper publishes http://antares.protres.ru/fold-amyloid/ -- NOT the bioinfo.protres.ru host this project checked. Both return 000 over http and https, as does the amyloid_base.html dataset page. Dead or blocked from this host is still undecided. (2) THE METHOD IS NOT GONE. It is fully specified: three 20-value amino-acid scales (expected packing density; backbone-backbone H-bond probability by donor; the same by acceptor), sliding window 5 residues, a region called amyloidogenic when at least 5 consecutive residues exceed the cutoff, cutoffs 21.4 contacts/residue, 0.697 donor, 0.671 acceptor, 0.090 twice-hybrid and 0.062 triple-hybrid, and hybrids built by z-normalising each scale to mean 0 and sd 1 then averaging with equal weights. The ONLY missing piece is the 20 numeric values per scale: Figure 1 plots them as bar charts and the text refers the contact scale to Galzitskaya et al. 2006a. So FoldAmyloid is reimplementable, and the legacy baseline is three-of-four runnable rather than two-of-four.
entries.found_in: PDF supplied by the author, 15 Nov 2026
entries.note: THREE THINGS THAT DEVALUE A FOLDAMYLOID NEGATIVE, all READ from the paper. (a) IT MISSES VQIVYK. 'In the case of unstructured tau-protein, only contact scale finds the experimentally detected (von Bergen et al., 2000) region (306-311)' -- two of three scales miss the canonical steric zipper. The abstract's '10 out of 11' is reached twice by different routes: the packing-density scale gets 10/11 missing a myoglobin fragment, and the acceptor scale -- the best performer on peptides -- gets 10/11 by missing tau PHF6. No single scale reaches 11. (b) THE DECISION UNIT IS FIVE RESIDUES: window 5, reliable frame 5, call on 5 consecutive residues above cutoff. This is primary-source support for the project's spine, that a negative call on a 25-residue proline- and charge-rich turn is uninformative by construction. (c) THE TAXONOMY HAS NO CATEGORY FOR OUR REGIONS. The paper names type I (hydrophobic) and type II (Gln/Asn-rich, GNNQQNY), states that 'most methods of prediction of amyloidogenic fragments are designed for searching for the regions of type I', and that 'our database contains no amyloidogenic peptides of the second type'. A proline- and charge-rich region is neither type.
entries.CONTAMINATION_2026_11_15: THE TRAINING SET IS NOW CHARACTERISED, closing a gap recorded in psychiatric_crossbeta_survey.md. 407 peptides, 144 amyloidogenic and 263 non-amyloidogenic, merged from Fernandez-Escamilla et al. 2004 (TANGO's OWN paper) and Thompson et al. 2006 (AmylHex, the 3D-profile paper). The two free parameters, cutoff and sliding-window size, were OPTIMISED ON THAT SET, so the headline 80 percent / 72 percent is in-sample. Table 2's head-to-head is worse: its 179 peptides are 'in fact a third of our database', i.e. a SUBSET of FoldAmyloid's own tuning set, while TANGO's row comes from a set derived from TANGO's own paper and PASTA's row is taken from PASTA's own paper (Trovato et al. 2007). The whole table spans sensitivity 0.73-0.79 and specificity 0.73-0.79; at n<=179 the binomial standard error on any one value is roughly +/-0.04 to 0.06, so THE ENTIRE PUBLISHED COMPARISON IS ABOUT ONE STANDARD ERROR WIDE and no method in it is distinguishable from another. Same conclusion as the CANYA result already in STATE.md, now reachable from a 2010 primary source.

entries.citation: Basha S, Nadkarni PP, Pai AR, Mahato KK (2026). Co-aggregation of amyloidogenic proteins in age-related neurodegenerative diseases. Ageing Research Reviews 118:103148. doi:10.1016/j.arr.2026.103148. Open access, CC BY.
entries.claim_as_cited: Candidate source on protein co-aggregation, adjacent to this project's DISC1/CRMP1/TRIOBP-1/NPAS3 co-aggregation claim.
entries.action: READ IN FULL 15 Nov 2026. PRE-EMPTS NOTHING, and it is NOT obtain-list item 8 (that is the Cells 2023 review 'Co-Aggregation and Parallel Aggregation of Specific Proteins in Major Mental Illness', which this paper does not cite). Scope is Tau, alpha-synuclein, Abeta and TDP-43 only. DISC1, TRIOBP, CRMP1, NPAS3 and dysbindin appear NOWHERE in it. USE IT FOR FOUR THINGS, listed in the note field. DO NOT MINE IT FOR VALIDATION ROWS -- see the warning field.
entries.found_in: PDF supplied by the author, 15 Nov 2026
entries.note: FOUR USES. (a) THE CO-OCCURRENCE/INTERACTION DISTINCTION, now citable from the neurodegeneration field. Fischer et al. 2025, quoted in the review: p-Tau and p-alpha-syn 'frequently accumulate in the same brains', but 'direct colocalization within Lewy bodies or neurites is rare, with Tau typically surrounding but not overlapping alpha-syn', so 'spatial co-existence does not always imply direct physical interaction'. The review adds its own: co-localization in the same inclusion 'does not automatically specify the temporal order of events or the structural organization of the aggregate core'. This is exactly the Q5 finding in triobp_crmp1_npas3_dysbindin.md, reached independently. (b) A PUBLISHED TAXONOMY our co-aggregation claim should be placed in: Bondarev et al., Int J Mol Sci 19:2292 (2018) distinguishes TITRATION, SEQUESTRATION, AXIAL and LATERAL co-aggregation, each with different functional consequences and different intervention strategies. Our DISC1/CRMP1/TRIOBP-1 claim does not say which it is. (c) THE SEEDING-ASSAY GAP IS REINFORCED. Seed amplification assays and RT-QuIC are clinical-grade in this field -- CSF SAA in a longitudinal AD cohort (Franzmeier 2025), alpha-syn RT-QuIC as a differential diagnostic (Quadalti 2021), Tau biosensor seeding on brain extracts (Tome 2023) -- and have never been pointed at psychiatric tissue. (d) POSITIONING. A 2026 comprehensive review of protein co-aggregation with over 300 references cites ZERO psychiatric co-aggregation work. The DISC1/TRIOBP literature is invisible to the field that owns the concept.
entries.WARNING_DO_NOT_MINE_FOR_ROWS: Its residue-level detail looks rich and is almost entirely SIMULATION-DERIVED, so under the found_by column nearly every region in it is CIRCULAR for a predictor benchmark. Tau PHF6/PHF6* and the Y310 'hotspot' with Abeta16-22: replica-exchange MD. Abeta E3-H6, K16-E22, I31-A41 and hIAPP N20-T30: all-atom explicit-solvent REMD. TDP-43 G287/G288 and alpha-syn A18/T22 interface: computational mutagenesis plus MD. alpha-syn NAC domain with hIAPP: MD. Abeta42 with the TDP-43 amyloidogenic core region: discrete MD. The two experimental exceptions worth chasing are Sun et al., J Biol Chem 301:108351 (2025) -- cryo-EM alpha-syn 'strain B', critical C-terminal segment D105-E115 -- and Yin et al., Cell Death Discov 11:76 (2025) -- PS1 cleaves TDP-43 at residue 315, biochemical.
entries.QUALITY_FLAGS: It calls itself systematic -- 'Literature for this review was systematically accumulated from PubMed and Google Scholar using targeted keyword combinations' -- but gives NO search strings, NO date window, NO inclusion criteria and NO PRISMA. It is a narrative review, so ITS NEGATIVES CANNOT BE CITED AS EVIDENCE OF ABSENCE. Section 3.2 asserts that research on Abeta/alpha-syn co-aggregation 'lacks scientific evidence' and then runs roughly fifteen rhetorical questions as content. Roughly eight self-citations to the corresponding group. ChatGPT and Grammarly use is disclosed for language editing, and some sentences do not parse, e.g. 'leading to progressive neurodegeneration and translating tauopathy therapeutics from discovery to clinical application'.

_the_flagship_study_is_a_different_one: Nucifora et al., Am J Psychiatry (2019): 42 schizophrenia against 41 controls, prefrontal cortex and superior temporal gyrus, three brain banks, cold sarkosyl fractionation, mass spectrometry on the insoluble pellet; 20 of 42 cases carried elevated insoluble and ubiquitinated protein. The MS is reported AT PATHWAY LEVEL ONLY -- no named protein list, no fold changes, no FDR were found. Full text not retrievable (cookie wall, 403, paywall), so even the 42/41/20 counts are second-hand. This supplement is the highest-value outstanding retrieval in the whole group.
_the_strongest_contrast_has_no_published: Zaharija et al., IJMS 23(19):11048 (2022): insoluble TRIOBP-1 in 12 of 25 schizophrenia, 15 of 25 major depression, 2 of 50 controls, anterior cingulate. Called significant with NO p-value published for the headline comparison. Computed here from those counts: schizophrenia against control, Fisher exact p = 1.2e-05, odds ratio 18.0 (95% CI 4.1 to 79.4); depression against control, p = 1.4e-07, odds ratio 28.6 (95% CI 6.4 to 127.5). Those are strong, and they are the best case-control contrast in this literature -- but the counts are second-hand and the paper also prints an impossible p-value, '3.7 x 10^4', evidently a typo. Verify the counts against the PDF before any use.
_the_measurement_that_changes_the_framin: Aggregates isolated from schizophrenia, bipolar and depression brain tissue are reported NOT to stimulate thioflavin T fluorescence, while recombinant DISC1 C-region fibrils do. If that holds, the honest statement is not 'the patient structure is not yet determined' but 'the patient-tissue species is not established to be an ordered amyloid at all', and no coordinate-based method can be validated against tissue. It INVERTS the Alzheimer and Parkinson situation, where both forms are dye-positive and the surprise was that the folds differ. Read as a statement inside Cukkemane 2025 attributing it to Leliveld 2009 and Korth 2012; primary sources returned 403. A dye negative in a dilute extract can also be a sensitivity failure. NOT load-bearing until verified at primary level.
_what_has_never_been_tried: No seeding assay has ever been run on psychiatric brain homogenate, although FRET biosensor and RT-QuIC assays are routine on post-mortem tissue in tau and alpha-synuclein. There is no published negative either, so 'not seeding-competent' and 'never tested' are currently indistinguishable. Cheap to answer and nobody has.
_the_arithmetic_that_blocks_it_first_IS_: The arithmetic holds: C680, C682 and C684 do lie outside the 691-836 fibril-forming construct, confirmed against the UniProt sequence (678-690 = KLCSCKCPLLGKV). The CONCLUSION drawn from it does not. The construct is NOT cysteine-free -- it carries C698, C762 and C782, and C762 sits immediately downstream of the reported beta-core boundary at 761. So a cysteine question inside the aggregating region does exist. What does not exist is any evidence for it: no source tests disulfide formation in DISC1, no source implicates oxidative conditions in its aggregation, both Cukkemane papers used no reducing agent and never mention disulfides, and the triad's only characterised function is arsenous-acid chelation through FREE thiols, which argues against disulfide bonding. 9RUX models the homologous mouse cluster with no disulfide, but the triad is not conserved in mouse (C-x-C, not C-x-C-x-C), so that structure cannot settle it either.
_the_core_range_is_contested_by_a_second: bioRxiv 10.1101/2023.08.03.551216 reports that NO single D, I, S or C region of DISC1 aggregates on its own in cells, and localises aggregation instead to a roughly 30-residue CENTRAL D-I LINKER, explicitly contrasting this with the C-terminal in vitro result. Both groups acknowledge the conflict. Note the shape of it: the TRIOBP-1 aggregation-critical region is likewise a 25-residue LINKER between the first two coiled coils, and was likewise missed by every predictor. Two coiled-coil scaffold proteins, two inter-domain linkers, two prediction failures -- that is a hypothesis with two independent points, and it is testable by a benchmark without any structure at all.
_the_one_computable_question_2026_11_15: Do the human-conserved triad thiols C682/C684 support disulfide formation or oxidation, and at what energetic cost? Input is PDB 9RUX (released 2026-05-06; Zhou et al., Nat Commun 2026), a 3.9 A cryo-EM homotetramer of MOUSE Disc1 322-722 that resolves the counterparts of human C682 and C684 at 6.70-8.10 A SG-SG. Cluster sizes measured from the coordinates: 618 atoms at 12 A, 754 at 14 A, inside the budget. It has wet-lab validation to be falsified against -- Watanabe et al. 2023 (Front Mol Biosci) show As(OH)3 binds the C-X-C-X-C motif with ALL THREE cysteines required, binding capacity 95+/-6% for wild type against 17+/-4% for the triple C->S mutant, which is the classical assay for clustered, reduced, accessible thiols. And NO quantum-chemical thiol-disulfide, cysteine-oxidation or disulfide-stability calculation exists for DISC1 or for ANY psychiatric-associated protein, at any level of theory: three structured queries returned only materials science, surface chemistry and non-psychiatric biology. The route is unoccupied.
_what_that_computable_question_does_NOT_: Two limits that must travel with it. FIRST, it is chemistry on the FOLDED protein, not on an aggregate interface: the triad sits outside both the 691-836 fibril construct and the reported 716-761 beta-core. That is the same distinction as tau PHF6 against the real Alzheimer interface, and it must be stated rather than blurred. SECOND, it does not explain the motivating phenotype: the ~200-230 kDa dopamine-induced high-molecular-weight DISC1 band, the only dopamine-dependent species ever measured, appears on gels whose stated sample buffers contain 8% beta-mercaptoethanol, so it is probably not disulfide-linked at all. Honest framing: a computable redox-switch question on a folded deposited domain, not a computation of psychiatric aggregation.
_S704C_is_closed_for_redox: Measured from 9RUX coordinates, not inferred. The mouse equivalent S701 is resolved in all four chains and is buried -- 96 neighbour heavy atoms within 8 A, contacting W393 and L349 -- and there is NO cysteine SG within 11.76 A of it in any chain. Both conditions for a redox role fail: not exposed, and no reachable partner. S704C is a folding and packing variant. Do not spend CPU on it.
_a_species_artefact_that_would_have_look: 9RUX's prettiest feature is mouse-only. Mouse C668 and C695 sit at 3.81-4.08 A SG-SG, reproduced across all four chains -- a textbook reduced near-disulfide about 1.8 A from bonding. Mouse C668 corresponds to human Y671, so the pair DOES NOT EXIST in human DISC1. Computing it would be mouse biology presented as human disease. Related brake: side-chain B-factors at these cysteines are 105-116 at 3.9 A, so the SG positions are modelled rather than observed and carry angstrom-scale uncertainty against a 2.05 A target bond. Any calculation must SCAN the SG-SG coordinate rather than trust the deposited geometry. And the protein was purified in 1 mM DTT at every step, so the structure says nothing about cellular redox state.
_the_uncontrolled_variable_nobody_has_ch: The 691-836 fibril construct contains three free cysteines (C698, C762, C782), and across Cukkemane 2021, Cukkemane 2025 and Zhou 2026 there is ZERO mention of DTT, TCEP, mercaptoethanol, reducing conditions, disulfide or redox. Those fibrils were therefore grown from a three-cysteine construct in air with the thiol oxidation state uncontrolled and unreported. Non-reducing against reducing SDS-PAGE would settle it in an afternoon and nobody has run it. This is a WET-LAB question, not a computation -- and it is the kind of specific, cheap, decisive question worth putting to an experimental group. Unverified for Narayanan 2011 (Europe PMC returned HTTP 500) and Leliveld 2009; established for the other three.

samardzija2025thesis.citation: Samardzija B (2025). Aggregation, parallel aggregation and co-aggregation of proteins in chronic mental illnesses. PhD thesis, University of Rijeka, Faculty of Biotechnology and Drug Development. Mentor: Nicholas J. Bradshaw. Defended 5 June 2025. 274 pp. urn:nbn:hr:193:966004
samardzija2025thesis.provenance: READ. Supplied by the author 15 Nov 2026 after both recorded biotech.uniri.hr URLs returned HTTP 404 and repository.biotech.uniri.hr returned HTTP 418 to scripted requests. Obtained by asking, not by retrieval.
samardzija2025thesis.why_it_was_tier_0: It was the single named threat to the project's novelty claim: a thesis from the group that mapped the DISC1 and TRIOBP-1 aggregation-critical regions is exactly where unpublished modern-predictor runs would sit, unindexed by PubMed and Europe PMC. PREREGISTRATION.md section 11 listed it as a falsification condition.
samardzija2025thesis.VERDICT: GAP HOLDS. No aggregation predictor run of any kind appears in the thesis. Methods 3.1-3.19 contain no bioinformatics section. Named software is instrumentation or statistics only: ImageLab, CellSens, ImageJ/Fiji, JASP, Prism, MassHunter, FlyTracker/MATLAB, a Python social-interaction-network script, BioRender, and ProSite used solely to draw the domain cartoons of Figures 2 and 3. TANGO, AGGRESCAN, FoldAmyloid, ProA, WALTZ, PASTA, AmylPred2, AggreProt, AggrescanAI, protein language models and AlphaFold are all absent. The one 'in silico' phrase concerns CRMP1 missense variants and cites Ravindran et al. 2022.
samardzija2025thesis.what_it_adds_1_NUMBERING_CONFLICT: p.48 states the TRIOBP-1 critical 25 aa sequence was 'later shortened to the 7 aa domain'. data/regions.json carries 333-340, which is 8 residues, sourced to Zaharija et al. 2022 IJMS 23:11048, on which this thesis author is a co-author. One of the two is wrong by one residue. This moves a Tier A boundary and must be settled before the freeze.
samardzija2025thesis.what_it_adds_2_NEW_PAPER: Reference 502: Zaharija B & Bradshaw NJ (2024), 'Aggregation of Disrupted in Schizophrenia 1 arises from a central region of the protein', Prog Neuropsychopharmacol Biol Psychiatry 130:110923. Not previously in this register. The thesis uses its Flag-DISC1 257-655 construct ('D and I domain only'). Experimental region-mapping of DISC1 aggregation by the same group; a candidate Tier A row, possibly better sourced than the unverified 384-415. Check found_by for circularity before use.
samardzija2025thesis.what_it_adds_3_DISEASE_CONTRAST: The thesis reports aggregation of DISC1, CRMP1 and TRIOBP-1 in control individuals as well as patients, region-specific rather than uniform, with the HIGHEST DISC1 aggregation signal of any group found in CONTROLS (lateral orbitofrontal gyrus). The author states that earlier studies pooled all CMI patients against controls and that the phenomenon is a subset, not a diagnosis marker. This does not affect our benchmark, which scores predictors against fragment-level mapped regions and not against disease association, but it forbids describing these in print as 'the schizophrenia aggregates'.
samardzija2025thesis.what_it_does_NOT_give: No new fragment-level mapped region. No TRIOBP-1 25-mer sequence. No DISC1 384-415 range. It confirms only the frames: TRIOBP-1 '593 or 652 aa' (p.47) and DISC1 854 aa (p.38). The section 6.3 freeze blockers survive untouched.

zaharija2022.citation: Zaharija B, Odorcic M, Hart A, Samardzija B, Marreiros R, Prikulis I, Jukovic M, Hyde TM, Kleinman JE, Korth C, Bradshaw NJ (2022). TRIOBP-1 Protein Aggregation Exists in Both Major Depressive Disorder and Schizophrenia, and Can Occur through Two Distinct Regions of the Protein. Int J Mol Sci 23:11048. doi:10.3390/ijms231911048
zaharija2022.provenance: Publisher PDF supplied by the author. Open access (MDPI, CC BY).
zaharija2022.VERDICT: SETTLES THE 7-vs-8 CONFLICT AT EIGHT, AND CLEARS THE TRIOBP-1 HALF OF PREREGISTRATION §6.3. regions.json was right; the 2025 thesis was wrong by one.
zaharija2022.what_it_adds_1_LENGTH_SETTLED: EIGHT residues, stated three times: abstract ('just 8 amino acids (333-340 of the 652 amino acid-long TRIOBP-1)'), discussion p.13 ('just 8 amino acids (AA 333-340)'), Figure 6D legend ('narrow the critical region to AA 333-340'). The 2025 thesis p.48 'later shortened to the 7 aa domain' is a slip.
zaharija2022.what_it_adds_2_SEQUENCE_READ: Figure 1B prints ELEKL|PLRENKRVPLTALLNQSRGERRGPP|SDGHE under a 324-348 numbering row, five flanking residues either side. Reproduces the previously DERIVED 25-mer byte-for-byte. Alignment confirmed by two independent composition checks: 333-340 = LTALLNQS (zero charges; the paper calls it 'the uncharged region') and 341-345 = RGERR (the paper calls it 'the cluster of charged amino acids beginning at AA 341'). Range read at §2.2 p.6. The 48.0% gatekeeper figure is no longer a reconstruction.
zaharija2022.what_it_adds_3_CONSTRUCT_CONFLICT: Figure 6B legend restates 324-328 as 'essential for aggregation' citing Bradshaw 2017, while Figure 3D of this same paper shows 333-652 aggregating indistinguishably from 324-652 and the text concludes 'the first cluster of charged amino acids is not required for aggregation'.
